insights.topic: Verified purchase data vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl's cryptographically verified receipts represent a structurally different signal class than cookie-based inference — 107,549 confirmed purchase events across $5.15M cumulative GMV means every record is a closed transaction, not a behavioral guess.

insights.topic: Grocery vertical depth and brand coverage
insights.insight: Six distinct grocery brands have crossed the activity threshold — Walmart, Kroger, Costco, Publix, Whole Foods, and Trader Joe's — spanning mass-market through premium tiers, giving marketers a rare cross-segment view of verified grocery spend in a single data layer.

Four new metro cells were added on 2026-11-25 alone — the highest single-day expansion on record — including a simultaneous double-cell pulse that suggests regional cluster thresholds being crossed rather than individual market onboarding; New York-Newark entered the prior cycle.

insights.topic: Unknown category as high-value signal gap
insights.insight: The 'Unknown' category carries an average ticket of $87.79 per receipt versus $44.27 for grocery — nearly double — meaning a material share of the highest-value transactions in the dataset are currently unclassified and represent an unresolved attribution opportunity for brand marketers.

insights.topic: 7-day GMV recovery pattern confirms purchase cadence
insights.insight: Post-UTC-rolloff recovery across six consecutive intervals — from a $66.8K trough back to $74.3K within 16 hours — demonstrates a predictable daily purchase rhythm, which gives media planners a structural basis for timing campaign attribution windows.

insights.topic: Financial services and logistics confirmed alongside core retail
insights.insight: Chase (23 receipts) and The UPS Store both hold positions in the thresholded brand list alongside grocery and department store anchors, confirming that verified commerce data here spans financial transactions and fulfillment touchpoints — not just point-of-sale retail.
